extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, institutional counsel, and stakeholders (students, advisors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory standards interpreting §106.46 and related Title IX provisions for how postsecondary institutions must structure and conduct grievance procedures (advisors, attendees, expert witnesses, evidence access, timeframes, privacy/FERPA considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to an advisor of choice (may be an attorney)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.46(e)(2) specifies that a party's advisor of choice may be an attorney and the advisor is not required to be an attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The status of a party's advisor (e.g., whether an attorney) and the financial resources of any party must not affect the institution's compliance with §§106.45 and 106.46, including obligations to objectively evaluate relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence, treat parties equitably, and use unbiased investigators and decisionmakers. The regulations do not require institutions to pay for parties' legal counsel or advisors, but nothing precludes an institution from choosing to do so or from offering attorney- or non-attorney-advisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions may restrict advisor participation but restrictions must be equal and consistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may establish restrictions on the extent to which an advisor may participate in grievance proceedings; such restrictions are a permitted part of adjudicative process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions on advisors are permissible to ensure orderly and efficient proceedings, but any restrictions must apply equally to both parties. If an institution permits questioning by an advisor at a live hearing under §106.46(f)(1)(ii)(B), the institution must allow the party's advisor of choice to conduct the questioning. The final regulations do not prescribe specific types of restrictions or functions advisors may perform; those determinations are left to the institution's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisor presence — cannot be limited from attending meetings or proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution must not limit the presence of the advisor for a complainant or respondent in any meeting or proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While institutions can restrict participation, they cannot bar the advisor from attending. If a party refuses to attend and thus refuses to answer relevant questions, a decisionmaker may weigh that party's statements less (§106.46(f)(4)), but must not draw an inference about whether sex-based harassment occurred solely from the party's refusal to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions are not required to pay for parties' advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to pay for parties' legal counsel or advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although institutions are not required to fund advisors, they may choose to do so or offer advisors voluntarily. The financial ability of a party must not affect the institution's compliance with evaluation and fairness obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee as advisor — voluntary choice allowed; institution-appointed confidential employees prohibited for live-hearing questioners
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may choose a confidential employee to serve as their advisor of choice, but a postsecondary institution may not appoint a confidential employee to serve as the institution-appointed advisor when the institution is required to appoint an advisor to ask questions on behalf of a party at a live hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring a confidential employee to serve as an institutional advisor may jeopardize their confidential role and risk disclosure of communications otherwise protected under §106.45(b)(7)(i). If a party voluntarily selects a confidential employee as advisor, the Department accepts the attendant confidentiality risks. §106.46(f)(1)(ii)(B) was revised to bar appointment of confidential employees as institution-appointed questioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisor who is also a witness — allowed; decisionmaker may consider conflicts and influence
rubrics_metrics.description: A party may select an advisor who has served or may serve as a witness in the grievance proceedings; institutions should permit this selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisionmakers may consider potential conflicts of interest or whether the advisor-witness was exposed to information in their role as advisor that could influence their testimony. Institutions may advise parties about potential complications of selecting an advisor who might be called as a witness.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prohibition on advisors with academic/professional authority over another party
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary or appropriate to prohibit an advisor who has academic or professional authority over another party from serving as an advisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will not limit the party's right to select an advisor with whom the party feels most comfortable; potential authority relationships are not viewed as inherently jeopardizing evidence reliability or proceeding integrity. Institutions may, however, place equal restrictions on advisors' participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions not required to mandate advisor training
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to mandate training for advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring mandatory advisor training could limit parties' ability to select an advisor based on the advisor's receipt of such training. Institutions are not prohibited from offering training for advisors voluntarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable extensions of timeframes for advisor availability and good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §106.46(e)(5), institutions must allow reasonable extension of timeframes on a case-by-case basis for good cause while remaining mindful of obligations to meet reasonably prompt timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for accommodations of an advisor's availability should be handled under the institution's reasonable-extension authority, balancing promptness and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisor may ask questions at live hearing even if party absent; weight of statements may be affected
rubrics_metrics.description: If a live hearing is used, each party has a right to have their advisor ask relevant and not otherwise impermissible questions and follow-ups; a party retains the right to have their advisor ask questions even if the party chooses not to appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party refuses to respond by not attending, §106.46(f)(4) permits a decisionmaker to place less or no weight on that party's statements, but the decisionmaker must not infer whether sex-based harassment occurred solely from the absence. Parties may request live hearings with parties in separate locations under §106.46(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons other than advisors may be permitted at institution's discretion (§106.46(e)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions have discretion to permit persons other than the party's advisor to attend meetings or proceedings, but must provide the same opportunities to parties and interpret this discretion consistent with FERPA and other laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions do not have to allow parents, support persons, or others; presence of additional individuals must not violate FERPA. GEPA (§106.6(e)) does not override FERPA to permit persons whose presence would violate FERPA. If any student or participant whose PII would be disclosed provides prior written consent, FERPA concerns can be addressed. Union representatives may accompany parties if FERPA is not implicated. Institutions must also consider ADA/Section 504 (auxiliary aids, reasonable modifications) and Title VI language assistance — in some cases another person present may be necessary to ensure effective participation, and the GEPA override would apply to permit such attendance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No required limit on number of accompanying persons or mandatory confidentiality agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to specify a limit on the number of persons who may accompany a party or to require confidentiality agreements, leaving these determinations to institutional discretion in light of FERPA and privacy obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.45(b)(5) requires reasonable steps to protect privacy during grievance procedures; institutions may choose confidentiality agreements or other steps if appropriate to protect privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional discretion to allow expert witnesses (§106.46(e)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institutions have discretion to decide whether expert witnesses will be permitted in a particular case involving sex-based harassment allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert witnesses may be unnecessary or prolong proceedings; institutions should decide based on facts/circumstances, balancing promptness, fairness, and accuracy. Institutions must exercise discretion in a manner that complies with duties to objectively evaluate relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence, treat parties equitably, and use unbiased investigators/decisionmakers. Parties may explain why expert testimony would be helpful. Parties retain opportunity to present fact witnesses and other relevant evidence. Character witnesses are permitted only as relevant and not otherwise impermissible under §106.45(f)(2). The Department will not require a blanket right to experts as under the 2020 amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to 'relevant and not otherwise impermissible' evidence — evidence option or investigative report option (§106.46(e)(6)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must provide parties and their advisors an equal opportunity to access the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence either by: (a) providing access to the underlying evidence (evidence option) or (b) providing access to a written investigative report that accurately summarizes that evidence (investigative report option).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an institution initially chooses the investigative report option and a party requests access to the underlying evidence, the institution must provide the underlying relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence to all parties. Institutions are not required to give physical or electronic copies but must provide an equal opportunity to access the materials. The scope is 'relevant' (as defined in §106.2) rather than the broader 2020 'directly related' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on access to complainant's sexual predisposition/prior sexual conduct evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not permit parties to have access to evidence regarding a complainant's sexual interests or prior sexual conduct except where that evidence falls within two narrow §106.45(b)(7)(iii) exceptions: (1) offered to prove someone other than the respondent committed the alleged conduct, or (2) evidence about specific incidents of the complainant's prior sexual conduct with the respondent offered to prove consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a narrowing from the 2020 amendments which had a broader 'directly related' inspection right; parties therefore will not have broad access to sexual-history evidence unless it meets an exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance definition and limits on institutional discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department added a definition of 'relevant' in §106.2 to limit recipient discretion and clarify that relevant evidence is evidence related to the allegations and that may aid a decisionmaker in determining whether the alleged sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department rejects the view that the relevance standard gives too much discretion; a decisionmaker may not rely on evidence to which the parties were not given access. Under §106.46(h)(1)(iii), the written determination must include the decisionmaker's evaluation of the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative reports — optional but must be accurate and accompanied by access upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions may provide an investigative report summarizing the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence instead of immediate access to the underlying evidence, but the report must accurately summarize the evidence and the institution must provide underlying evidence if requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some commenters urged requiring investigative reports; the Department allows either option but requires parity: if an investigative report is used and a party requests the underlying evidence, the institution must provide equal access to the underlying evidence to all parties.
